text: Stores product category definitions and metadata for organizing inventory items.
Associative table linking customers to their demographic profiles, facilitating many-to-many relationships between customer records and customer type definitions.
Stores demographic profile information and descriptions for customer segments or types.
Stores master data for customers including contact details, business information, and shipping addresses.
Stores detailed personal and professional information about company employees, including contact details, job roles, and reporting hierarchies.
Maps employees to their assigned sales territories, establishing the many-to-many relationship between the Employees and Territories tables.
A junction table linking orders to specific products, recording the quantity, price at time of sale, and any discounts applied for each line item.
Stores order transaction details including dates, shipping information, customer and employee identifiers, and freight costs.
A master table containing detailed information about all products available for sale, including their identification, supplier, category, pricing, stock levels, and discontinuation status.
Stores definitions for geographic regions used to group territories. Acts as a lookup table for regional categorization.
Stores information about shipping companies or logistics providers used for delivering orders.
Stores detailed contact and location information for product suppliers, including company names, addresses, and key personnel.
Stores geographic territory data including descriptions and their associated regions.
Unique integer identifier for each product category, serving as the primary key and foreign key reference in the Products table.
Textual name of the product category, such as Beverages or Confections.
Detailed textual description explaining the contents or scope of a specific product category.
Binary large object storing the visual logo or image associated with a specific product category.
Unique identifier for a customer, serving as the primary key in this table and referencing the Customers table to identify the specific customer entity.
Unique identifier for a customer demographic type, referencing the CustomerDemographics table to classify the customer's market segment or profile.
Unique identifier for a specific customer demographic type or segment, serving as the primary key.
Text description detailing the characteristics or definition of the associated customer demographic type.
Unique identifier for each customer record.
Name of the customer's business or organization.
Name of the primary contact person for the customer.
Job title or role of the primary contact person within the company.
Street address of the customer's location.
City where the customer is located.
Geographic region or state/province where the customer is located.
Postal or zip code for the customer's address.
Country where the customer is located.
Contact telephone number for the customer.
Facsimile number for the customer.
Unique identifier for each employee in the system.
The last name or surname of the employee.
The first name or given name of the employee.
The job title or position held by the employee within the organization.
The courtesy title or salutation used for the employee (e.g., Mr., Ms., Dr.).
The date of birth of the employee.
The date when the employee was hired by the company.
The home address of the employee.
The city where the employee resides.
The region or state of residence for the employee.
The postal or ZIP code associated with the employee's residence.
The country where the employee is located.
The home telephone number of the employee.
The internal phone extension number for the employee.
Binary large object containing the employee's profile photograph.
Additional notes or biographical information regarding the employee.
The EmployeeID of the manager to whom this employee reports.
The URL or file path linking to the employee's photo.
Identifies the specific employee associated with a territory assignment.
Identifies the specific sales territory assigned to the employee.
The unique identifier for the parent order associated with this line item.
The unique identifier for the product sold in this order line.
The price of a single unit of the product at the time the order was placed.
The number of units of the product purchased in this order line.
The discount percentage applied to this specific line item, ranging from 0 to 0.25.
The unique identifier for a specific order.
The unique identifier linking the order to a specific customer.
The unique identifier of the employee who processed or handled the order.
The date and time when the order was placed.
The date by which the customer expects the order to be delivered.
The date and time when the order was actually shipped or dispatched.
The ID of the shipper or carrier company responsible for delivering the order.
The shipping cost or freight charges associated with a specific order.
The name of the customer or company to whom the order is being shipped.
The full street address where the order is to be delivered.
The city where the order is to be delivered.
The region, state, or province of the delivery destination.
The postal or zip code for the delivery address.
The country where the order is to be delivered.
The unique identifier for each product entry in the database.
The name or title of the product.
A foreign key linking the product to its corresponding supplier in the Suppliers table.
A foreign key linking the product to its corresponding category in the Categories table.
The specific packaging unit or quantity description for the product (e.g., case size, weight per pack).
The price of a single unit of the product.
The current number of units of this product available in the inventory.
The number of units of this product that have been ordered from the supplier but have not yet arrived.
The minimum inventory level threshold at which a new order for this product should be placed.
A flag indicating whether the product has been discontinued (e.g., '1' for discontinued, '0' for active).
Unique integer identifier for each geographic region. Serves as the primary key for the Regions table and foreign key in Territories.
Textual name or label describing the geographic region, such as Western, Eastern, Northern, or Southern.
Unique identifier for a shipping company.
The name of the shipping company or carrier.
Contact phone number for the shipping company.
Unique identifier for each supplier in the system.
The full legal name of the supplier company.
The name of the primary contact person at the supplier's organization.
The job title or role of the contact person within the supplier's company.
The street address of the supplier's physical location.
The city where the supplier is located.
The region, state, or province where the supplier is located.
The postal or ZIP code for the supplier's location.
The country where the supplier's business is based.
The primary phone number for contacting the supplier.
The fax number associated with the supplier's business contact.
The website URL or homepage link for the supplier's company.
Unique identifier for a specific sales territory.
Textual description of the territory, often representing a city or local area.
Foreign key linking the territory to its parent region.
